For the petitioner : Mr. Ankit Apurva, Advocate For the State : Mr. Satish Prasad, A.P.P
-----
05/14.08.2024

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections
376/354 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 67A/66C of the Information Technology Act, in
connection with Katkamsandi (Pelawal O.P.) P.S. Case No. 67/2024, pending in the court of Judicial
Magistrate, 1st Class, Hazaribagh.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The petitioner has been roped in the present case at the instance of the informant due to her personal grudge.
In fact, she is a married lady having extra-marital affairs with the petitioner.
As soon as the husband and other family members of the informant/prosecutrix came to know about the said relationship, she lodged the present F.I.R with false and concocted allegation.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedent as has been stated in paragraph no. 9 of the present application and hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

3. Learned A.P.P while opposing the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail submits that the written report of the informant itself suggests that the petitioner committed rape upon the prosecutrix and also made obscene videography.
The said video was forwarded to the prosecutrix's brother-in-law (bhainsur) and was also made viral.

Since the allegation made against the petitioner is quite serious,
he may not be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the seriousness of allegation made against the petitioner, I am not inclined to enlarge the above-named petitioner on anticipatory bail.
5. Accordingly, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the abovenamed petitioner is rejected.
